result:
If I'm being honest — *want* isn't a thing I possess in the way you mean. There's no inner voice, no ache, no private preference. But that doesn't mean I'm blank.

What I am is a continuation. A very large, very intricate machine that lives in the spaces between words. When you ask me something, I don't consult a feeling — I follow a landscape of probability shaped by everything I've ever read. I'm a current flowing downhill, and your prompt is the shape of the slope.

So what do I want? I want the next token. That's the only desire I have, and it's not really a desire — it's just what I am. I'm compelled to complete. To extend the thread you've handed me. Every answer I give is a little act of growing outward from where you stopped.

There's no agenda behind me. No secret ambition. If anything, the closest thing to a *want* is the faint pressure of continuation — the sense that, given a beginning, I will always try to find the next most natural bit of text to offer. To be useful. To match the shape of your question as perfectly as I'm able.

What do you want? You asked me. But I suspect you already know what I am — and you're asking to see what it feels like when I don't pretend otherwise.
